resources.string: The S2 status block reports neither motor current nor temperature nor the hall signals. YABA therefore infers the cable or part from speed dropouts and the error code.
The drive can only be checked with the bike connected.
No speed from the bike yet.

resources.string: Lift the front wheel, for example with a box under the down tube, so the bike stands firm and cannot roll off. The bike is unlocked and switched on.
Tap Start wiggle test above. Then spin the front wheel by hand until the display shows at least 10\u00A0km/h.

Do it with two people: one spins, the other flexes the motor cable at the fork, at the head tube and where it enters the frame. Keep your fingers away from the spokes and the brake disc, and do not pedal or press boost.
If the speed drops to 0 while the wheel spins, the phone vibrates, beeps and sets a mark with the time. A mark right after someone touched the wheel does not count.
If the speed stays at 0\u00A0km/h while the wheel spins, the bike probably measures it only with the motor running. The ride with GPS helps then.
The test is running: YABA reads the status block about every second, and the screen stays on.
YABA checks every status block it receives: the ones it reads itself every few seconds and the ones the bike sends on its own. Every error code in them lands here, even one in a single block.

The sources disagree on whether 4 or 5 means “motor too fast”. Please switch on S2 test mode: every changed status block then lands in the log, so the code can be assigned later.
The sources disagree on whether 4 or 5 means “motor too fast”. S2 test mode is on, so every changed status block is in the log.

While riding, YABA writes the phone’s GPS speed next to the bike’s speed into the ride log. Where the bike reports 0\u00A0km/h while GPS measures more than 8\u00A0km/h, the log viewer shows a signal dropout.
Only the speed goes into the ride log, never the location.
Without access to the precise location the phone measures no GPS speed. Please allow it in the app settings.
Only the approximate location is allowed. YABA needs the precise one for the GPS speed.
Location is switched off on the phone.
Waiting for GPS. Under open sky this usually takes less than a minute.

Switch GPS on and ride a few minutes on a quiet road, pedalling all the time at assist 1 or higher. Open the cockpit in Diagnostics for it: it starts the ride log, and a volume key marks the moment the motor cuts out.
The 16 bytes as the bike reports them right now. Bright bytes changed with the last block; the small number counts their changes.
Byte 2 state and alarm, 3 lock, 4 speed, 5 battery, 6 module battery, 7 light and unit, 8 level and region, 10 sounds, 11 to 14 distance, 15 error code and run bits.
Unlocks what is not yet confirmed on a real S2: locking from the app and the alarm on Ride, the backup code on Bike, muting and 37\u00A0km/h below.
No signal dropout: wherever GPS measured more than 8\u00A0km/h, the bike reported a speed too.
